verdict.rationale: Gmail API supports OAuth scopes with explicit guidance to use narrow, non-sensitive scopes to limit access to only what's needed (gmail-docs-4, gmail-docs-29), which enables scoped credential issuance for third-party/agent apps. However, this is generic OAuth scoping rather than a purpose-built agent-credential or fine-grained per-action permission system, and there's no evidence of dedicated tooling for issuing/revoking agent-specific least-privilege tokens (e.g., no API keys, no per-agent scoping UI). Missing for 10: agent-specific credential issuance workflow, evidence of granular per-action permissions beyond broad scopes, independent confirmation that scoping is effectively least-privilege in practice.
